parsed.summary: This paper evaluates the feasibility of using quadruped robots, specifically the Unitree Go2, for tasks in roof environments. It identifies significant challenges such as slippage, dynamic stability, and control limitations, and provides a baseline for future research. The study highlights the need for tailored locomotion strategies and hardware adaptations for successful deployment in roof environments.

chk_problem.value: Feasibility of deploying quadruped robots for construction work on roofs.
chk_problem.paper_quote: This paper investigates the feasibility of deploying quadruped walking robots for the automation of work in roof environments.

chk_method.value: Systematic experimental evaluation of the Unitree Go2 quadruped robot on a roof test rig.
chk_method.paper_quote: A dedicated test rig of a roof’s surface was designed to evaluate the baseline performance of a commercial quadruped, the Unitree Go2, in this new environment.

chk_data.value: Data collected from experiments on a roof test rig using the Unitree Go2 robot and OptiTrack motion capture system.
chk_data.paper_quote: To objectively evaluate and compare quadruped locomotion, an accurate measurement methodology is required. In this work the main focus is placed on friction as the primary performance indicator, while loss of stability, referred to as critical failure, marks the upper performance limit when the robot falls.

chk_setup.value: Adjustable roof test rig with Frankfurter Pfanne tiles, OptiTrack motion capture system, and controlled experiments with the Unitree Go2 robot.
chk_setup.paper_quote: To objectively assess the performance of the Go2 (software version 1.4.4) and create a baseline for future comparison with custom feet, an adjustable test rig of a roof environment was developed (see Fig. 1).

chk_primary_result.value: Critical failure during incline walking at 25°; measured friction coefficients of 1.144 ± 0.1299 (flat) and 1.430 ± 0.1298 (curved).
chk_primary_result.paper_quote: The coefficient of friction for a rubber ball foot on a roof tile was measured at 1.144 ± 0.1299 on flat and 1.430 ± 0.1298 on curved sections of the roof.

chk_secondary_result.value: Quadratic relationship between slippage and incline angle; dynamic locomotion limited by stability, control, and material friction.
chk_secondary_result.paper_quote: Regression analysis revealed a highly significant (p < 0.0035) linear relationship between incline angle and traveled distance, a highly significant (p(F ) < 0.001) quadratic relationship between incline angle and slippage, but no explainable correlation between incline angle and trajectory deviation.

chk_baseline.value: Baseline performance of Unitree Go2 robot on roof test rig with standard ball feet.
chk_baseline.paper_quote: This work provides the first systematic assessment of quadruped locomotion in roof environments, highlighting both the potential and the current limitations of this application and establishes a baseline for future research.

chk_conclusion.value: Quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe and reliable operation on roofs without significant adaptations.
chk_conclusion.paper_quote: These results underscore that, without appropriate adaptations, quadrupeds are not yet capable of safe and reliable operation in roof environments.

chk_limitation.value: Experiments were conducted under ideal conditions with a single robot model and standard settings.
chk_limitation.paper_quote: Lastly, all experiments have been conducted under ideal conditions, no additional debris, vegetation, weather or additional payloads were added.
